test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at X% above the cost price and sells them at a discount of 48%. If he makes a profit of 82%, find the value of X.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct ratio formula between Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP):

MP/CP = (100 + Profit%)/(100 − Discount%)

MP/CP = (100 + 82)/(100 − 48) = 182/52 = 3.5/1

Mark-up % (X) = (Ratio − 1) × 100

X = (3.5 − 1) × 100 = 250%

**∴ The correct answer is 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount % = 48%

Profit % = 82%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100

MP = SP × 100 / (100 − D%)

Mark-up % (X) = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/496a7885da66cd688938534900039357eedff1cafd14da8eb0dbb19f72e5a46e.png] 

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100 units

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = CP + 82% of CP

⇒ SP = 100 + 82 = 182 units

⇒ SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

⇒ 182 = MP × (100 − 48)/100

⇒ 182 = MP × 52/100

⇒ MP = (182 × 100) / 52

⇒ MP = 350 units

⇒ Mark-up = MP − CP = 350 − 100 = 250 units

⇒ X% = (Mark-up / CP) × 100

⇒ X% = (250 / 100) × 100 = 250%

**∴ The correct answer is 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

The most efficient way to link mark-up, discount, and profit is: MP/CP = (100 + P%)/(100 − D%).

Successive Percentage Method

Profit % can be calculated using the net effect of mark-up (m) and discount (d): Net % = m − d − (md/100).

Mark-up Calculation

Mark-up value is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP), whereas Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP).
